mechanics:
**Mechanics** — motion and forces, the largest and most predictable part of EJU physics.

**Covers**: kinematics, forces & equilibrium, Newton's laws, work–energy, momentum, circular motion, simple harmonic motion and gravitation.

**On the EJU**: the biggest source of marks — master free-body diagrams, the three conservation laws (energy, momentum) and equation of motion, and most of mechanics falls out.
thermodynamics:
**Thermodynamics** — heat, temperature and gases.

**Covers**: heat/temperature and specific heat, latent heat, the gas laws and equation of state, kinetic theory, and the first law across the standard state changes (isochoric/isobaric/isothermal/adiabatic).

**On the EJU**: calorimetry, ideal-gas calculations and $p$–$V$ processes recur every year — learn the four processes and the first law cold.
waves:
**Waves** — oscillations that carry energy.

**Covers**: wave properties, superposition/interference/standing waves, sound (strings, air columns, beats, resonance), the Doppler effect, geometric optics (lenses/refraction) and light interference (Young, gratings, thin films).

**On the EJU**: standing waves, Doppler and interference (path difference) are staples — the key is always the path/phase difference condition.
electromagnetism:
**Electricity & Magnetism** — charges, fields, circuits and induction.

**Covers**: electric field/potential, capacitors, DC circuits, magnetic fields and forces, electromagnetic induction, AC and (briefly) semiconductors.

**On the EJU**: circuit analysis, capacitor energy, the Lorentz force and Faraday/Lenz induction are heavily tested — keep signs and directions straight.
atomic-physics:
**Atoms** — modern physics: quantized light and matter.

**Covers**: the photoelectric effect and photons, wave–particle duality, the Bohr model and atomic spectra, nuclei/decay/half-life, and elementary particles.

**On the EJU**: photoelectric equation, energy-level transitions and half-life calculations are the usual questions.
kinematics:
**Description of motion** — position, velocity, acceleration.

**Key formulas** (constant $a$): $v=v_0+at$, $x=v_0t+\tfrac12at^2$, $v^2=v_0^2+2ax$.
- Free fall: $a=g$ downward. Projectile: horizontal $a=0$ (constant $v_x$), vertical is free fall — treat the axes independently.
- Relative velocity: $\vec v_{AB}=\vec v_A-\vec v_B$.

**On the EJU**: read $v$–$t$ graphs (slope $=a$, area $=$ displacement), projectile range/height, relative motion.

**Watch out**: keep $x$ and $y$ separate in projectiles; they share only the time $t$.
forces:
**Various forces** — the pushes and pulls in a problem.

**Core ideas**
- Gravity $W=mg$; normal force ⟂ to surface; tension along a string; friction opposes relative sliding; elastic (spring) force $F=kx$; buoyancy $F=\rho V g$ (weight of displaced fluid).

**On the EJU**: correctly draw every force on a free-body diagram before writing equations.

**Watch out**: the normal force is *not* always $mg$ (e.g. on an incline $N=mg\cos\theta$, or with an extra applied vertical force).
force-equilibrium:
**Equilibrium of forces** — when a body doesn't accelerate.

**Key idea**: net force $=0$ → resolve into components: $\sum F_x=0$ and $\sum F_y=0$.
- Resolve each force along convenient axes (often along/perpendicular to an incline).

**On the EJU**: hanging masses, objects on inclines, three-string junctions.

**Watch out**: choose axes that simplify the algebra (align one axis with the incline or the unknown).
rigid-body:
**Rigid-body equilibrium & torque** — rotation balance.

**Key formulas**: torque $\tau=Fd$ (force × perpendicular distance to the pivot). Equilibrium: $\sum F=0$ **and** $\sum\tau=0$.
- Centre of mass is where gravity effectively acts; a couple is two equal opposite forces giving pure rotation.

**On the EJU**: ladders, hinged beams, balancing — take torques about a clever pivot to remove an unknown.

**Watch out**: use the *perpendicular* distance (lever arm), not the along-force distance.
newtons-laws:
**Laws of motion** — Newton's laws.

**Key formula**: $\vec F_{\text{net}}=m\vec a$ (equation of motion).
- 1st: no net force → constant velocity. 3rd: forces come in equal-and-opposite pairs on *different* bodies.

**Method**: draw the FBD → write $F=ma$ along each axis → solve.

**On the EJU**: connected bodies (strings/pulleys), inclines, lifts/elevators.

**Watch out**: action–reaction pairs act on different objects, so they never cancel on the same body.
friction-resistance:
**Motion with friction / air resistance**.

**Key ideas**
- Static friction $f\le\mu_s N$ (adjusts up to a max); kinetic friction $f=\mu_k N$ (constant, opposes motion).
- With air resistance (∝ speed), a falling body reaches **terminal velocity** when drag $=mg$ (so $a=0$).

**On the EJU**: "does it slip?" thresholds, blocks on inclines, terminal-velocity reasoning.

**Watch out**: check whether the object is actually moving — use $\mu_s$ (a limit) if static, $\mu_k$ if sliding.
work-energy:
**Work and kinetic energy**.

**Key formulas**: $W=Fd\cos\theta$; power $P=\dfrac{W}{t}=Fv$; kinetic energy $K=\tfrac12mv^2$.
- Work–energy theorem: net work $=\Delta K$.

**On the EJU**: work done by/against a force, power of a motor, speed changes via work–energy.

**Watch out**: only the force component *along* the displacement does work; a perpendicular force (e.g. normal, centripetal) does zero work.
potential-energy:
**Potential energy & conservation**.

**Key formulas**: gravitational $U=mgh$; elastic $U=\tfrac12kx^2$.
- Conservation of mechanical energy (no friction): $K+U=\text{constant}$.
- With friction: $\Delta(K+U)=-(\text{energy lost to friction})$.

**On the EJU**: ramps, pendulums, spring launches — set two states equal.

**Watch out**: choose one reference height for $U$ and use it consistently; include friction losses when present.
momentum-impulse:
**Momentum, impulse & collisions**.

**Key formulas**: $\vec p=m\vec v$; impulse $=\vec F\,\Delta t=\Delta\vec p$.
- Momentum is conserved in any collision (no external force): $\sum p_{\text{before}}=\sum p_{\text{after}}$.
- Coefficient of restitution $e=\dfrac{\text{separation speed}}{\text{approach speed}}$; elastic $e=1$ (KE conserved), perfectly inelastic $e=0$ (stick together).

**On the EJU**: 1-D collisions, explosions, restitution off a wall.

**Watch out**: momentum is a *vector* — keep signs by direction; KE is conserved only when $e=1$.
circular-motion:
**Uniform circular motion**.

**Key formulas**: $v=r\omega$; period $T=\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$; centripetal acceleration $a=\dfrac{v^2}{r}=r\omega^2$; centripetal force $F=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$.

**Core idea**: the net inward force *is* the centripetal force — identify what provides it (tension, gravity, friction, normal).

**On the EJU**: conical pendulum, vertical loops, banked/curved tracks.

**Watch out**: "centripetal force" is a role, not a new force — don't add it on top of the real forces.
inertial-force:
**Inertial / centrifugal force** — physics in an accelerating frame.

**Key idea**: in a frame accelerating with $\vec a$, add a fictitious inertial force $-m\vec a$ to every body, then treat the frame as if static.
- Centrifugal force $\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$ outward is the inertial force in a rotating frame.

**On the EJU**: objects inside accelerating vehicles or on rotating platforms.

**Watch out**: inertial forces exist *only* in the non-inertial frame; from the ground frame use real forces + centripetal acceleration instead.
shm:
**Simple harmonic motion**.

**Key idea**: a restoring force $F=-kx$ gives SHM with period $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$ (spring) or $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\ell}{g}}$ (simple pendulum).
- $x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi)$, $\omega=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$; speed is max at the centre, zero at the ends; acceleration is max at the ends.

**On the EJU**: period of springs/pendulums, energy exchange $K\leftrightarrow U$, position/velocity at a given phase.

**Watch out**: period is independent of amplitude (for ideal SHM).
gravitation:
**Universal gravitation**.

**Key formulas**: $F=G\dfrac{Mm}{r^2}$; gravitational PE $U=-G\dfrac{Mm}{r}$; circular orbit: $\dfrac{GMm}{r^2}=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$.
- Kepler: orbits are ellipses; equal areas in equal times; $T^2\propto r^3$.

**On the EJU**: satellite/orbital speed and period, Kepler's third law, escape ideas.

**Watch out**: orbital $U$ is negative and uses $1/r$ (not $mgh$, which is only near a surface).
heat-temperature:
**Heat and temperature**.

**Key formulas**: heat $Q=mc\,\Delta T$ (specific heat $c$); heat capacity $C=mc$.
- Absolute temperature $T(\mathrm K)=t(^\circ\mathrm C)+273$.
- Calorimetry: heat lost by hot = heat gained by cold (conservation of heat).

**On the EJU**: mixing substances at different temperatures to find the final temperature.

**Watch out**: include the container's heat capacity when given, and use consistent units.
states-latent-heat:
**States of matter & latent heat**.

**Key idea**: during a phase change the temperature stays constant while heat is absorbed/released — $Q=mL$ (latent heat of fusion/vaporization).
- A full heating curve alternates $Q=mc\Delta T$ (sloped) with $Q=mL$ (flat).

**On the EJU**: total heat to melt-then-heat-then-boil; reading heating/cooling curves.

**Watch out**: don't use $mc\Delta T$ during a phase change — $\Delta T=0$ there; use $mL$.
heat-work-laws:
**Heat, work & the laws of thermodynamics**.

**Key formula (1st law)**: $\Delta U=Q+W_{\text{on gas}}$ (or $\Delta U=Q-W_{\text{by gas}}$).
- Internal energy depends only on temperature (for an ideal gas). Heat-engine efficiency $\eta=\dfrac{W}{Q_{\text{in}}}=1-\dfrac{Q_{\text{out}}}{Q_{\text{in}}}$.
- 2nd law: heat won't flow cold→hot on its own; $\eta<1$.

**On the EJU**: apply the first law to each process; compute efficiency.

**Watch out**: fix your sign convention for $W$ and use it consistently.
ideal-gas:
**Ideal-gas equation of state**.

**Key formulas**: $PV=nRT$; Boyle ($T$ const): $PV=$const; Charles ($P$ const): $V/T=$const; combined $\dfrac{PV}{T}=$const.

**On the EJU**: relate two states of a gas; find $n$, $P$, $V$ or $T$; mixtures via partial pressures.

**Watch out**: temperature must be **absolute (K)**; watch units of $P$ and $V$ so they match $R$.
gas-molecules:
**Motion of gas molecules** (kinetic theory).

**Key ideas**: pressure comes from molecular collisions; average translational KE $=\tfrac32kT$ (∝ absolute temperature).
- Internal energy: monatomic $U=\tfrac32nRT$; diatomic $U=\tfrac52nRT$.

**On the EJU**: link temperature to molecular speed/energy; internal energy of monatomic vs diatomic gases.

**Watch out**: use $\tfrac32nRT$ only for *monatomic* internal energy; diatomic has extra (rotational) modes.
gas-state-change:
**Changes of state of gases** — the four processes.

**Key facts** (first law $\Delta U=Q-W_{\text{by}}$, $\Delta U\propto\Delta T$):
- Isochoric ($V$ const): $W=0$, $Q=\Delta U$.
- Isobaric ($P$ const): $W=P\Delta V$.
- Isothermal ($T$ const): $\Delta U=0$, so $Q=W$.
- Adiabatic ($Q=0$): $\Delta U=-W$ (compressing heats the gas).

**On the EJU**: read $p$–$V$ diagrams (area $=$ work) and apply the first law per process.

**Watch out**: molar specific heat differs at constant $P$ vs $V$ ($C_P=C_V+R$).
wave-properties:
**Properties & propagation of waves**.

**Key formula**: $v=f\lambda$; period $T=1/f$.
- Transverse (⟂ oscillation, e.g. light) vs longitudinal (∥ oscillation, e.g. sound).
- On a $y$–$x$ graph read $\lambda$; on a $y$–$t$ graph read $T$.

**On the EJU**: extract $\lambda$, $f$, $v$ from a graph or description; direction of medium motion.

**Watch out**: don't confuse the wavelength graph ($y$ vs position) with the period graph ($y$ vs time).
wave-superposition:
**Superposition, interference & standing waves**.

**Key ideas**: waves add (superpose). Constructive when path difference $=m\lambda$; destructive when $=(m+\tfrac12)\lambda$.
- Two identical opposite waves → a standing wave with fixed nodes/antinodes; spacing between adjacent nodes $=\lambda/2$.
- Reflection: fixed end inverts (phase flip); free end does not.

**On the EJU**: interference conditions and standing-wave patterns.

**Watch out**: a fixed-end reflection adds a half-wavelength phase shift — include it in path-difference conditions.
sound:
**Sound: strings, air columns, resonance**.

**Key formulas**: string/open pipe fundamental $f=\dfrac{v}{2L}$; closed pipe $f=\dfrac{v}{4L}$ (odd harmonics only). Beats: $f_{\text{beat}}=|f_1-f_2|$.

**On the EJU**: resonance lengths, harmonics of open/closed pipes, beat frequency, string tension effects ($v=\sqrt{T/\mu}$).

**Watch out**: a closed pipe has a node at the closed end and only *odd* harmonics; include end corrections only if asked.
doppler:
**Doppler effect** — frequency shift from motion.

**Key formula**: $f'=\dfrac{v\pm v_o}{v\mp v_s}\,f$, where $v$ is sound speed, $v_o$ observer, $v_s$ source.
- Approaching raises pitch, receding lowers it. Choose signs so "approach → higher $f$".

**On the EJU**: moving source and/or observer; reflection off a moving wall (apply Doppler twice).

**Watch out**: the source term is in the *denominator*, observer in the numerator — set signs by whether they approach or recede.
light:
**Light: reflection, refraction, lenses**.

**Key formulas**: Snell $n_1\sin\theta_1=n_2\sin\theta_2$; total internal reflection when $\sin\theta_c=\dfrac{n_2}{n_1}$; lens/mirror $\dfrac1a+\dfrac1b=\dfrac1f$, magnification $m=-\dfrac{b}{a}$.

**On the EJU**: refraction angles, critical angle, image position/size for lenses and mirrors, dispersion.

**Watch out**: use a consistent sign convention (real image $b>0$); light bends *toward* the normal entering a denser medium.
light-interference:
**Diffraction & interference of light**.

**Key formulas**: double slit bright fringes at $d\sin\theta=m\lambda$, fringe spacing $\Delta y=\dfrac{L\lambda}{d}$; grating $d\sin\theta=m\lambda$.
- Thin film / air wedge: constructive/destructive from the optical path difference (watch the half-wave phase shift on reflection off a denser medium).

**On the EJU**: Young's fringe spacing, grating angles, thin-film colours.

**Watch out**: include the $\lambda/2$ shift only when reflecting off a *higher*-index medium — it flips constructive ↔ destructive.
electric-field:
**Electrostatic force & electric field**.

**Key formulas**: Coulomb $F=k\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2}$; field $E=\dfrac{F}{q}=k\dfrac{Q}{r^2}$ from a point charge.
- Fields (vectors) from several charges add by superposition; field lines go + → −.

**On the EJU**: net force/field from a charge arrangement; where the field is zero.

**Watch out**: add fields as *vectors* (components), not magnitudes; note like charges repel.
electric-potential:
**Electric potential**.

**Key formulas**: point-charge potential $V=k\dfrac{Q}{r}$ (scalar); PE $U=qV$; work $W=q\,\Delta V$; uniform field $E=\dfrac{V}{d}$.

**On the EJU**: potential from several charges (just add), energy to move a charge, field–potential relation.

**Watch out**: potential is a *scalar* (add with signs, no components); a charge moves toward lower PE.
conductors-dielectrics:
**Matter in electric fields**.

**Key ideas**: in a conductor, charges rearrange (electrostatic induction) so the interior field is zero (shielding) and the surface is an equipotential.
- A dielectric polarizes, weakening the field inside and *raising* a capacitor's capacitance.

**On the EJU**: induced charge, shielding, and the effect of inserting a dielectric.

**Watch out**: field inside a conductor in equilibrium is zero; a dielectric increases capacitance by a factor of its permittivity.
capacitors:
**Capacitors**.

**Key formulas**: $Q=CV$; parallel-plate $C=\varepsilon\dfrac{S}{d}$; energy $U=\tfrac12CV^2=\tfrac12QV$.
- Series: $\dfrac1C=\sum\dfrac1{C_i}$ (same charge). Parallel: $C=\sum C_i$ (same voltage).

**On the EJU**: series/parallel combinations, stored energy, effect of a dielectric or changing plate separation.

**Watch out**: series capacitors share the *charge*; parallel share the *voltage* — opposite to resistors' intuition.
dc-circuits:
**Direct-current circuits**.

**Key formulas**: Ohm $V=IR$; power $P=VI=I^2R$; Joule heat $Q=I^2Rt$. Series $R=\sum R_i$; parallel $\dfrac1R=\sum\dfrac1{R_i}$.
- Kirchhoff: currents in = out at a node; voltages around a loop sum to zero. EMF with internal resistance $r$: terminal $V=\varepsilon-Ir$.

**On the EJU**: solve multi-loop circuits, power dissipated, internal-resistance effects.

**Watch out**: apply Kirchhoff carefully with consistent current directions/signs.
semiconductors:
**Semiconductors**.

**Key ideas**: n-type (extra electrons, donor) and p-type (holes, acceptor). A p–n junction conducts in forward bias only → a diode (rectifier).

**On the EJU**: identify carrier type, forward/reverse bias, and diode behaviour in simple circuits.

**Watch out**: current flows across a p–n junction in the forward direction only.
magnetic-field:
**Magnetic fields from currents**.

**Key formulas**: straight wire $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$; solenoid $B=\mu_0 n I$ ($n$ = turns per length).
- Direction by the right-hand rule.

**On the EJU**: field magnitude/direction near wires, coils and solenoids; superposition of fields.

**Watch out**: distance dependence differs — $1/r$ for a straight wire, roughly uniform inside a long solenoid.
magnetic-force:
**Magnetic force & Lorentz force**.

**Key formulas**: force on a current $F=BIL\sin\theta$; on a charge $F=qvB\sin\theta$ (Lorentz), directed by the right-hand/left-hand rule.
- A charge in a uniform $B$ moves in a circle: $qvB=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$ → $r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$.

**On the EJU**: force between parallel currents, radius/period of a charged particle, Hall effect.

**Watch out**: the magnetic force is always ⟂ to velocity → it does no work and only changes direction.
em-induction:
**Electromagnetic induction**.

**Key formulas**: Faraday $\varepsilon=-\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$ ($\Phi=BA$); moving rod $\varepsilon=BLv$.
- Lenz: the induced current opposes the change in flux.

**On the EJU**: emf from a changing field/area, sliding-rod problems, direction of induced current, self/mutual induction.

**Watch out**: the induced current's direction *opposes* the flux change (Lenz) — get the sign/direction right.
ac-circuits:
**Alternating current & EM waves**.

**Key ideas**: AC $v=V_0\sin\omega t$; effective (rms) value $V_{\text{rms}}=\dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt2}$.
- Reactances: inductor $X_L=\omega L$, capacitor $X_C=\dfrac1{\omega C}$; resonance when $X_L=X_C$.
- EM waves travel at $c=f\lambda$; the spectrum runs radio → γ.

**On the EJU**: rms values, reactance/impedance, resonance frequency, EM-wave basics.

**Watch out**: use rms (not peak) values for average power; $X_L$ and $X_C$ depend oppositely on frequency.
electrons-light:
**Electrons & wave–particle duality**.

**Key formulas**: photon energy $E=hf=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$; photoelectric $\tfrac12mv^2_{\max}=hf-W$ (work function $W$).
- de Broglie wavelength $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}$; light and electrons show both particle and wave behaviour.

**On the EJU**: photoelectric threshold and max KE, photon energy, de Broglie wavelength, X-rays.

**Watch out**: below the threshold frequency *no* electrons are emitted, regardless of intensity.
atoms-nuclei:
**Atoms and nuclei**.

**Key ideas**: Bohr model — electrons occupy discrete energy levels; a photon is emitted/absorbed when $hf=E_{\text{high}}-E_{\text{low}}$ (line spectra).
- Radioactive decay: activity halves every half-life $T_{1/2}$; remaining $=N_0(\tfrac12)^{t/T_{1/2}}$. Mass–energy $E=mc^2$.

**On the EJU**: spectral-line transitions, half-life calculations, decay types (α, β, γ).

**Watch out**: energy levels are negative and get closer together near $n=\infty$; use the *difference* for the emitted photon.
elementary-particles:
**Elementary particles**.

**Key ideas**: protons and neutrons are made of up (charge $+\tfrac23$) and down (charge $-\tfrac13$) quarks — proton = uud, neutron = udd. Four fundamental forces (strong, electromagnetic, weak, gravity).

**On the EJU**: light, mostly-conceptual — recognize quark composition and the fundamental forces.

**Watch out**: this topic is brief on the EJU; know the basic quark makeup and don't overinvest.
